title: Causal ingest checkpointing for metering consistency
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We observe duplicate billing events when edge proxies retry or resend requests after network partitions or timeouts. Existing solutions (opaque replay tokens, global nonces) reduce duplicates but have operational and latency costs when scaled across multi-region edge fleets. This ticket proposes a causal ingest checkpointing protocol: edges attach lightweight monotonic checkpoint tokens scoped to customer+edge-shard, and the ingestion plane performs conditional checkpoint commits to a strongly-consistent checkpoint ledger. The ledger stores the highest contiguous checkpoint per scope; any incoming request with a checkpoint <= ledger value is treated as already-accounted and short-circuited for metering. This provides deterministic duplicate suppression without requiring full request de-duplication at application layer.
design_notes: Data model: checkpoint key = <customer_id>::<edge_shard_id>. Checkpoint value = monotonic integer plus opaque epoch UUID to handle restarts. Storage: use a strongly consistent KV store (Spanner/CloudSpanner or CockroachDB) with Compare-And-Set (CAS) conditional writes to advance checkpoint. Edge responsibilities: stamp requests with next checkpoint, persist last-stamped checkpoint locally until commit confirmed. Server responsibilities: on ingest, attempt conditional commit; if commit succeeds, charge tokens and ack. If commit fails due to CAS, read current ledger and determine if incoming workload should be considered duplicate and return an idempotent ack. Batching: support batch checkpoint commits for multi-request batches by committing the highest sequence number in batch. GC: periodic background job to expire old checkpoint rows after long inactivity (configurable per-customer).
tradeoffs: Pros: deterministic suppression, low per-request metadata, works with at-least-once transports and multi-region edge fleets. Cons: requires strongly-consistent store or conditional writes (cost), introduces a small critical path on first commit (can be mitigated with async-ack for low-risk customers), needs careful handling for edge restarts to avoid gaps in sequence leading to false-duplication. Compared to global nonce approaches, this design reduces cross-region coordination by scoping to shard-level windows.
implementation_steps: 1) Schema + migration: add checkpoint ledger table with columns (scope, epoch, seq, last_updated, ttl). 2) Edge SDK: expose checkpointer abstraction to stamp requests and persist last-stamped token. 3) Ingest middleware: implement CAS commit flow and duplicate short-circuit path. 4) Backfill script: seed ledger for active customers to bootstrap. 5) Test harness: multi-region replay simulator and property tests. 6) Canary rollout and perf monitoring. 7) Full rollout with reconciliation sweeps enabled.
acceptance_criteria:
- End-to-end integration test demonstrates <=1 duplicates per 10M requests in the face of 5% edge retry rate.
- Metric 'metering.duplicate_count' decreases by at least 90% for canary customers compared to baseline.
- No customer-visible increase in p50 latency > 5ms for hosted API happy path.
- Rollback plan validated via canary failover to previous ingest behavior.
rollout_plan: Phase A (Canary): enable for internal sandbox customers and 1-2 low-traffic customers (1%) with full logging. Phase B: expand to 10% of traffic after 1 week of stable metrics. Phase C: 100% rollout with ledger GC and reconciliation jobs active. Each phase gated by duplicate_count, commit_conflict_rate, and p50 latency SLOs. Feature flag: ingest.checkpointing_v1.
monitoring_and_metrics: Essential metrics to add: metering.duplicate_count, metering.commit_conflicts, metering.commit_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), metering.reconciliation_actions, storage.cas_error_rate. Dashboards: link to Confluence design doc and Grafana: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/MET/Causal+Ingest+Checkpointing and https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd123/metering-checkpoints (placeholder). Alerts: fire if duplicate_count increases or commit_conflicts > 0.5% for 5min.
tests: Unit tests for CAS flow, integration tests with spanner emulator, chaos tests simulating edge restarts and partitioning, long-run duplicate rate load test (24h). Add golden baseline meter events for regression detection. Include post-deploy reconciliation smoke tests.
migration_plan: 1) Deploy ledger table schema as opt-in (feature flag off). 2) Run backfill for active customers in read-only; evaluate conflicts. 3) Enable canary customers with SDK changes. 4) Monitor and run reconciliation sweeps for customers with edge restarts. 5) Gradually flip feature flag across environments.
open_questions:
- Which strongly-consistent storage should we standardize on for ledger (Spanner vs Cockroach)? Cost/perf analysis required.
- Should we support edge-less customers (server-side only clients) with a virtual shard?
- TTL policy: what default expiry for inactive customers (90 days?) to balance table size and safe reboots?
- How does checkpointing interact with per-customer burst quota enforcement when checkpoints are advanced in batch?
